claims.statement: Psychiatry reaches most of what it studies through a person's account and through expressive behaviour such as speech and movement, so the separation between a symptom the patient reports and a sign the examiner observes cannot be applied as cleanly as it is in general medicine.
claims.scope: A methodological argument about psychiatric interviewing and about the nature of psychiatric symptoms and signs, made by phenomenologically oriented authors.
claims.uncertainty: The paper advances a position in a continuing methodological debate about structured versus semi-structured interviewing. The narrow point used here concerns how psychiatric phenomena are reached, which is not the contested part of that debate.

claims.statement: Reports about the same person from that person and from an informant commonly disagree, with correspondence typically in the region of a correlation of 0.2 to 0.4, and disagreement is not by itself evidence that either report is in error, because informants observe different contexts.
claims.scope: A review of multi-informant assessment across clinical science; most of the evidence it reviews concerns children and adolescents, and it reports that the pattern persists into middle age.
claims.uncertainty: The size of the correspondence varies with the characteristic assessed, the informant pair, and the measure used. The review reports it as a general pattern and not as a fixed value for any particular clinical question.

claims.statement: Which account is more accurate depends on what is being described: a person's own report carries more weight for internal states that cannot be observed from outside, and an informant's report carries more weight for outwardly visible and evaluative characteristics.
claims.scope: Evidence from a study of personality pathology in an adult sample, testing a self-other knowledge asymmetry model.
claims.uncertainty: The asymmetry was demonstrated for personality characteristics. Its size for symptom reporting in a clinical record is not established by this source, so the lesson uses it as a principle for deciding whom to ask rather than as a measured effect.

claims.statement: In a study of 23,630 inpatient progress notes written by 460 clinicians at one United States academic medical centre between January and August 2016, 18% of the text in a typical note had been entered manually, 46% was copied, and 36% was imported from elsewhere in the record.
claims.scope: One inpatient service, one electronic record system, and roughly eight months of 2016 at a single American academic centre.
claims.uncertainty: Documentation practice varies with record system, specialty, country, and year, so these proportions describe that setting rather than clinical records in general.

claims.statement: Diagnostic overshadowing is the misattribution of physical symptoms to a person's existing mental illness; a psychiatric history recorded in the chart is described as one of the conditions that predisposes clinicians to it, and reported consequences include worsening physical illness and death.
claims.scope: A concept analysis synthesising the diagnostic-overshadowing literature, drawn largely from high-income health systems.
claims.uncertainty: A concept analysis establishes a concept's antecedents and consequences as they appear in a literature; it does not measure how often overshadowing occurs. The mortality gap it cites for people with mental illness has several contributors, and the share attributable to overshadowing is not established.

claims.statement: In the World Health Organization's ICD-11 developmental field study, 339 clinicians assessed 1,806 patients across 28 sites in 13 countries under a joint-rater design, and intraclass kappa for agreement between the two clinicians ranged from 0.45 for dysthymic disorder to 0.88 for social anxiety disorder.
claims.scope: Adult patients in secondary and tertiary mental-health settings in the 13 participating countries, classified with draft ICD-11 diagnostic guidelines.
claims.uncertainty: Both clinicians observed the same interview, so the design excludes the variation that arises when clinicians take their own histories from the same patient. Agreement in ordinary practice would not be expected to exceed these values.

claims.statement: Whether depression is caused by lowered serotonin is actively disputed: a 2022 systematic umbrella review reported no consistent evidence of an association between serotonin and depression, and a 2023 reply in the same journal argued that the review's methods and reporting were flawed and that the serotonin system is implicated in depression.
claims.scope: The published exchange in Molecular Psychiatry between the umbrella review's authors and a group of critics.
claims.uncertainty: The lesson records only that the question is contested and takes no position on which reading of the evidence is correct. The exchange continued beyond these two papers, and neither settles whether antidepressant treatment works or how.

claims.statement: The 2022 umbrella review reports survey evidence that 80% or more of the general public believe it is established that depression is caused by a chemical imbalance.
claims.scope: Survey findings cited inside the umbrella review rather than measured by it.
claims.uncertainty: The surveys were conducted in particular countries and periods and are reported second-hand, so the figure indicates the scale of a widespread belief rather than a current measurement for any one population.

claims.statement: Fatigue, lethargy, cold intolerance, weight gain and constipation are the commonest symptoms of hypothyroidism in adults, and these features are non-specific: a case-control study found that none of 34 hypothyroidism-related symptoms could identify who had the condition, and 70% of people with normal thyroid function report one or more thyroid-associated complaints, so the diagnosis rests on biochemical testing.
claims.scope: A clinical review of hypothyroidism in adults; the two quantitative findings come from studies the review cites.
claims.uncertainty: Symptom frequency varies with age and with the degree of thyroid failure, and the review notes that the symptoms are especially non-specific in older people. Nothing here supports interpreting any individual person's symptoms.

terms.definition: The layer of a record that states what was reported and what was observed, without a conclusion about what any of it means. In this lesson it covers a person's report, another person's report, and direct observation.

In this lesson, the two kinds of statement that go furthest past a description: a classification and a causal explanation. Ordinary usage runs the word together with inference; this lesson keeps them apart because their checks differ.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 lists interpretation as an alias for inference, so in the premed corpus the two words name one thing. Psychiatry needs the word for something else: the classification and the causal explanation, which are conclusions of a different kind and are checked by agreement and by a named rival rather than by displaying their material. The prose bridges the two senses where the word is first reserved, and inference keeps its premed meaning unchanged.

terms.definition: A statement recorded because the person themself said it. Its check is to ask the person again, and its value depends on whether the person's own wording was kept.

A statement recorded because an informant, someone who knows the person and is speaking about them, said it. Its check is to ask that informant, and its weight depends on which parts of the person's life the informant actually sees.
A record of what an examiner saw or heard inside one bounded encounter, written so that another person present at the time could have agreed or disagreed. Its check expires when the encounter ends.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 owns observation as a record of what was noticed or measured, stated so that its object, conditions, and result can be checked. That meaning is kept and narrowed to the clinical encounter: the conditions are one bounded stretch of time with named people in the room, which is what makes the check a second person present at the time and what makes it expire.

terms.definition: A conclusion drawn from observations and reasoning rather than something recorded directly. Its check is to display the statements it rests on and see whether they carry it.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 owns this word and its meaning is kept unchanged. One thing does change: that lesson allows interpretation as an alias for inference, and this lesson does not carry the alias forward, because psychiatry needs interpretation to cover classification and causal explanation as well. Inference therefore stays narrow here and the two other kinds keep their own names.

terms.definition: A statement that a picture meets the requirements of a named category in a published set of diagnostic guidelines. Its check is agreement: whether a second clinician applying the same guideline reaches the same category.

A statement that one thing is producing or maintaining another. Its check is evidence that separates it from a named rival account, so a causal explanation with no rival named is not being checked at all.
The representation a causal explanation commits its writer to: which features of a situation are selected, which are treated as background, and which way the influence is asserted to run.

alignment.note: PREM-WEL-001 owns model as a purposeful representation of selected features and relationships used to explain, predict, or test within stated limits, and PREM-SCI-010 adopts it. That meaning is kept and narrowed to the small model implied by a single causal sentence in a clinical record, which is usually left unstated and which this lesson asks the writer to say out loud.

terms.definition: A number summarising how often two independent raters assign the same category, adjusted downwards for the agreement that guessing alone would produce. A kappa of 1 means they always agree and a kappa of 0 means they agree no more often than chance would arrange.
The misattribution of a person's physical symptoms to their existing mental illness, so that a physical cause is investigated less than it otherwise would be.

Continuity with earlier lessons

Three glossary entries relate to terms that published premed lessons already own, and each declares the relation in glossary.json and bridges it in the prose where the term first appears:

  • inference adopts the meaning owned by PREM-SCI-001, without carrying forward that lesson's interpretation alias.
  • interpretation is declared a distinct sense from the one PREM-SCI-001 implies by that alias: here it names the classification and the causal explanation, which are checked differently from an inference.
  • direct observation narrows the observation entry owned by PREM-SCI-001 to one bounded clinical encounter.
  • explanatory model narrows the scientific model entry owned by PREM-WEL-001 and adopted by PREM-SCI-010 to the small model implied by a single causal sentence in a record.
